# Bon Jovi Plays at Biden Event After Candidate Visits Bucks County

## While incumbent President Donald Trump was in North Carolina, Democratic candidate Joe Biden held drive-in rallies in Luzerne and Bucks counties in Pennsylvania Saturday.

#### By NBC Philadelphia Staff • Published October 24, 2020 • Updated on October 24, 2020 at 11:58 pm

NBC Universal, Inc.

“All eyes are on Pennsylvania,” former ambassador Nikki Haley tells NBC10’s Steven Fisher.

### What to Know

* Joe Biden, Donald Trump and their surrogates are keeping a presence in Pennsylvania in the final days leading up to the 2020 presidential election.
* Biden appeared in Bucks and Luzerne counties Saturday as Trump planned to visit North Carolina and the midwest.
* Former ambassador Nikki Haley spoke to Trump supporters in Norristown on Saturday.

Rock star Jon Bon Jovi gave a small concert at a drive-in rally in eastern Pennsylvania for Joe Biden on Saturday, performing three songs and praising Biden's response to the coronavirus.

The rocker took the stage in Dallas, Pennsylvania, wearing a black face mask that he peeled off to play acoustic versions of “Who Says You Can’t Go Home?,” “Livin’ on a Prayer” and “Do What You Can,” which was recently released and dedicated to those on the front lines of the coronavirus pandemic.

Bon Jovi also pulled out notes to praise Biden, saying, “I wrote my comments down because I’ve never played at a drive-in with all the horns honking, so it’s a little different.”

The rocker added that “Joe knows that masks are not a sign of weakness, they’re a sign of strength."

Delivering a speech a short time later as hundreds of cars honked their horns in approval, Biden said that Bon Jovi has “always gone wherever I’ve asked him” and called him a friend and “national treasure.”

Getty Images

Singer Jon Bon Jovi performs during a Biden-Harris Drive-In event at Dallas High School, in Dallas, Pennsylvania, on October 24, 2020. (Photo by Angela Weiss / AFP) (Photo by ANGELA WEISS/AFP via Getty Images)

Biden held two drive-in rallies in Pennsylvania on Saturday and has said for months he expects to win a state that could play a critical role in deciding next month’s election.

Dallas is in Luzerne County, where Donald Trump beat Hillary Clinton by more than 25,000 votes in 2016. Dallas isn't far from Scranton - where Biden lived as a child - in neighboring Lackawanna County, where Clinton eked out a victory of a few thousand votes in 2016.

Biden was in Pennsylvania as was Nikki Haley, speaking for Trump in Norristown. The president is coming to Allentown and Lancaster on Monday. NBC10's Drew Smith reports.

## Nikki Haley in Montco

Nikki Haley, the former ambassador to the United Nations, spoke for Trump at Montgomery County Community College in Norristown Saturday night.

Haley told NBC10's Steven Fisher: "all eyes are on Pennsylvania."

Earlier Saturday, Biden held a drive-in rally in Bristol where Trump supporters could be heard making a ruckus from a short distance away.

Bon Jovi’s New York fans were left wanting more when frontman Jon Bon Jovi ended the show early on Thursday, July 23, due to illness.

The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame-inducted band cut short their set at Madison Square Garden, the eighth in a nine-show stand, as the singer struggled with the effects of a sinus infection.

“Jon Bon Jovi spoke from stage and told fans he has been battling a sinus infection which led to the show’s early ending,” a rep for Bon Jovi tells *People*. “As part of the Bon Jovi residency at Madison Square Garden, Jon has said numerous times that it has been a joy to return to live shows for the band. Updated information will be available shortly.”

### Explore

According to reports, Bon Jovi completed 90 minutes of a set that featured a guest performance by Train’s Pat Monahan, who joined in for a version of the *Slippery When Wet* hit from 1986, “Livin’ On a Prayer.”

The dates are part of the band’s *Forever Tour*, presented by Live Nation, which represents a return to the road after Jon Bon Jovi underwent reconstructive surgery on his vocal cords and then a years-long rehabilitative process.

“Don’t throw away your ticket stubs I’m going to figure something out okay, don’t [fear],” Bon Jovi told the Garden, *People* reports. “Just hang onto it, I’m going to figure out how to reschedule.”

“I’m gonna have to cool it for a night,” he added, prior to exiting the stage. “I feel great, I’ll see you again soon, bye bye.”

Bon Jovi’s MSG run is scheduled to wrap this Sunday, July 26, after which time the band crosses the Atlantic for five stadium shows in Scotland, the Republic of Ireland and England, the final of which is booked for Sept. 9 at London’s Wembley Stadium, the last of three concerts at the venue.

Jon Bovi has been candid about his recovery, saying the band assembled every month to rehearse to gauge his progress, but that until he felt he could confidently sing through a two-and-a-half-hour show, they weren’t hitting the road.“Day to day, I’m working hard on it,” he told *Entertainment Tonight* in 2024. “Nothing else matters until I work on getting better. It’s up to God at this point. I’ve done everything I can do. I won’t fake it … the legacy matters too much.”
